name: Ajman Saray Resort
positioning: Ajman Saray, a Luxury Collection Resort: a beach resort on a private beach in Ajman, with Arabian Gulf and creek views from its balconies
best_for: Couples who want a private beach with Arabian Gulf sunsets
Families wanting two pools, a kids club and a beach
Spa-focused stays with a hammam experience

facts.text: Ajman Saray is set along a private beach in Ajman.
The hotel describes itself as the first beachside Luxury Collection Resort in the Middle East.
Rooms and suites have private balconies with Arabian Gulf or creek views.
Bathrooms have walk-in showers, bathtubs and Byredo amenities, and every room has Signature Luxury Collection linens.
Zihn Spa offers treatments including a hammam experience, along with a sauna and a steam room.
The resort has two swimming pools, one of them for children, steps from the beach.
The Kids Club has a kids pool, a playground, games and toys.
The fitness center has TechnoGym equipment and is open 24 hours a day.
Bab Al Bahr is a beachside bar and grill with Mediterranean-inspired dishes, handcrafted drinks and DJ music, plus a rooftop Sunset Lounge.
Escape Equestrian Bar is a quiet bar styled like an elegant members' club, known for signature cocktails.
Weddings and receptions can be held at an outdoor event space steps from the Arabian Gulf.
Self parking and valet parking are complimentary, and the resort is Green Key certified.

highlights.text: A white sandy private beach with an unobstructed view of the Arabian Gulf, a place to watch Ajman's sunset.
The Royal Suite looks over the Arabian Gulf and its beaches from both its living room and its balcony.
Zihn Spa's menu has seven signature healing journeys built around an energy-balancing concept, alongside a hammam experience.
A falcon show on the beach celebrates the place of falconry in Arab tradition and culture.
Ajman Museum, nearby, is housed in an 18th-century fort that was the ruler's residence until 1970.

considerations.text: Rooms do not have a fridge.
The closest airport is Sharjah International rather than Dubai International.
WhataHotel notes the resort is in quieter Ajman, so reaching Dubai attractions requires travel.
